skill.name: gitlab-ci-patterns

security_audit.summary: Static command and URL findings are false positives from markdown examples, inline code formatting, and reserved example.com placeholders. I found no prompt-injection or exfiltration intent, but two CI guidance issues need attention: disabled Kubernetes TLS verification and non-blocking high severity image scanning.

remediation.issue: Kubernetes deployment example disables TLS verification.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true and show CA certificate configuration through protected CI variables.

remediation.issue: Container vulnerability scan allows failures for high and critical findings.
remediation.suggestion: Make the scan blocking on protected branches, or document advisory-only behavior clearly.

semantic_findings.title: Kubernetes TLS Verification Disabled
semantic_findings.description: The deployment template uses --insecure-skip-tls-verify=true when configuring kubectl. This disables API server certificate validation and can permit traffic interception.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure flag appears directly in the deployment template. Legitimate self-signed testing is possible, but marketplace guidance should prefer trusted CA configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Security Scan Failures Are Allowed
semantic_findings.description: The Trivy job scans for high and critical image findings but allows the job to fail. This can let vulnerable images pass CI without enforcement.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scanner command targets HIGH and CRITICAL severities and the job sets allow_failure. Some teams may use advisory scans, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: GitLab pipeline design can become inconsistent across build, test, release, and infrastructure jobs. This skill provides practical CI/CD patterns for staged automation, caching, Docker publishing, deployments, Terraform, and security scanning.
actual_capabilities: Provides baseline GitLab CI stages for build, test, and deploy workflows.
Shows Docker image build and push jobs using GitLab registry variables.
Demonstrates staging and production Kubernetes deployments with manual production approval.
Includes Terraform validate, plan, and manual apply pipeline patterns.
Covers GitLab security templates, Trivy scanning, caching strategies, and dynamic child pipelines.
limitations: Examples need project-specific images, paths, variables, namespaces, and protected branch rules.
The package only includes SKILL.md; referenced asset and reference files are not present.
It does not validate generated YAML against a live GitLab instance.
It does not provision runners, cloud credentials, Kubernetes clusters, or Terraform backends.

use_cases.title: Launch application CI
use_cases.description: Create build, test, cache, coverage, and artifact jobs for a GitLab-hosted application.

use_cases.title: Standardize deployments
use_cases.description: Design staging and production deployment stages with GitLab environments and manual production approval.

use_cases.title: Extend platform automation
use_cases.description: Add Terraform, container scanning, dependency scanning, and child pipelines to an existing delivery workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitLab CI pipeline for a Node.js app with build, test, cache, coverage, and artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my GitLab CI pipeline to build a Docker image, tag it by commit, and push it to the GitLab registry.

prompt_templates.title: Design environment deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design staging and production GitLab deployment jobs for Kubernetes with protected variables, manual production approval, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a platform pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full GitLab CI pattern with Terraform validation, manual infrastructure apply, security scanning, caching, and dynamic child pipelines.

output_examples.input: Node.js service with linting, tests, coverage, and production release.
output_examples.output: A staged pipeline plan covering dependency installation, build artifacts, coverage reporting, cache keys, and a manual production deployment.

output_examples.input: Containerized app that deploys to staging and production Kubernetes namespaces.
output_examples.output: A deployment workflow with registry publishing, environment-specific jobs, protected variables, rollout checks, and production approval.

output_examples.input: Platform repository that manages Terraform and security checks.
output_examples.output: A CI structure with validation, planning, manual apply, scanning stages, cache guidance, and child pipeline placement.

best_practices: Replace placeholder URLs, namespaces, image names, and variables before committing generated pipelines.
Store secrets in GitLab CI/CD variables and use protected variables for production credentials.
Run generated YAML through GitLab CI Lint and test it on a non-production branch first.
anti_patterns: Copying example deployment targets directly into production repositories.
Using latest image tags for production jobs without pinning versions.
Running Terraform apply automatically without a manual approval gate.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete .gitlab-ci.yml file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft a complete pipeline, but you should adapt names, variables, secrets, and environments.

faq.question: Does it support Docker-in-Docker?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Docker build and registry push patterns using GitLab registry variables.

faq.question: Can it help with Kubernetes deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows deployment jobs, environment metadata, rollout checks, and manual production gates.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. It expects secrets to be stored in GitLab CI/CD variables or another approved secret store.

faq.question: Can it validate my pipeline?
faq.answer: It can review likely structure and risks, but GitLab CI Lint should validate syntax.

faq.question: Is it safe for production deployment design?
faq.answer: Use it as a starting point. Remove insecure flags, pin images, and test changes on protected branches.
